PullRequest.Title: sessions: Show catalog chats in the session list
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Show the default chat and lightweight peer-chat metadata from the Agent Host session catalog directly in the Agents Window session list.

- preserve the catalog's ordered chat identities, titles, origins, and interactivity without loading transcripts
- keep peer-chat facades stable while live session state enriches transient details
- resolve transient peer-chat details only while those observables are actively observed
- show nested chats expanded by default and persist explicit user collapse choices
- seed restored sessions from cached chat metadata and reconcile authoritative membership without collapsing or flickering
- preserve per-chat working directories added on main

The protocol support landed in microsoft/agent-host-protocol#455.

## Validation

- npm run compile
- npm run hygiene
- affected Agent Host state/service/provider and Sessions list unit suites: 1,058 passing, 27 pending

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The observer-to-lease call path, error callback, microtask retry, errored-entry eviction, and fresh wire subscribe/unsubscribe are all explicit in the code. Only the exact request rate varies with how quickly the host rejects requests.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Repeated session subscribe/unsubscribe IPC or network requests plus retry CPU work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost grows without bound with failure duration: while any peer-detail observable remains observed, every failed subscribe schedules the next attempt immediately, with no delay, cap, or cancellation beyond removing the observer.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Persistent failures cause excessive IPC/network traffic and CPU churn, reducing throughput and potentially keeping the Agents window busy.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, a session subscription error disposed the failed subscription and waited for an existing external trigger such as a visibility change, query, or reconnect before attempting another subscription; there was no observer-held immediate retry loop.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added onDidError branch now queues _ensureSessionStateSubscription in a microtask whenever the new peer-detail reference collection still has references.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 5892-5895 add queueMicrotask(() => { if (...hasReferences(sessionId)) { this._ensureSessionStateSubscription(sessionId); } }), converting an error into an immediate retry for as long as the newly introduced detail lease is held.
Findings.Title: Back off peer-detail resubscriptions after repeated failures
Findings.Impact: When a rendered peer chat keeps title/status details observed and the host persistently rejects or cannot serve the session subscription (for example during auth failure, a missing session, or a failing remote host), the client continuously creates subscriptions. AgentSubscriptionManager.getSubscription sends a fresh wire subscribe and disposal sends unsubscribe on every iteration, so a fast local failure can become a tight IPC loop and a remote failure becomes an indefinite request stream.
Findings.Evidence: AdditionalChat._withDetails acquires a lease for each observed detail, and the reference collection keeps hasReferences(sessionId) true until the row observer is disposed. AgentSubscriptionManager.getSubscription explicitly evicts errored entries and starts a fresh _subscribe request; disposing the provider store invokes unsubscribe. The added queueMicrotask path immediately calls _ensureSessionStateSubscription again after every onDidError, and the added test only proves one failure followed by success, not persistent failure behavior.
Findings.Recommendation: Replace the microtask retry with a cancellable bounded exponential backoff keyed by session, reset it after a successful snapshot or host reconnect, and cancel it when the last detail reference is released.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Repository-wide references show the Set is loaded, queried, added to, and deleted only on explicit expansion; the session-removal handler does not prune it. Magnitude depends on profile lifetime and user collapse habits, which is reflected in low severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Persisted session-resource strings, in-memory Set entries, and bytes serialized on each collapse-state write
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained state grows with the lifetime count of distinct nested sessions the user has collapsed, rather than with currently existing sessions; each later toggle copies and JSON-serializes the entire historical set.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded profile-state and memory growth, with increasing synchronous serialization/storage work on collapse toggles and list startup.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff there was no per-session collapse resource set, so deleted session identities were not retained or repeatedly serialized by the Sessions list.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new collapse persistence adds every collapsed session resource to a profile-scoped Set and only removes it if that same session is explicitly expanded; session removal does not evict the resource.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 5088 introduces insertion into collapsedSessionResources, while the added persistence implementation has no deletion/lifetime path for sessions that leave the catalog.
Findings.Title: Bound persisted collapse entries for removed sessions
Findings.Impact: Users who repeatedly collapse nested sessions and later delete them accumulate dead URI strings indefinitely. Over a long-lived profile, startup must parse all stale entries and every subsequent collapse/expand serializes and writes all retained identities, even though most can no longer affect the tree.
Findings.Evidence: saveSessionCollapseState adds resources at line 5088 and serializes the full Set at line 5093. The existing onDidChangeSessions removal branch at lines 3495-3508 refreshes the list and prunes section-order state, but never touches collapsedSessionResources. No other references to the new Set remove entries except expanding the same resource.
Findings.Recommendation: Bound the persisted state, for example with an LRU cap, and prune entries on confirmed permanent session deletion (not transient provider disappearance), then persist the compacted set once.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the Agents session list with catalog-backed chats
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing listSessions request and catalog/database reads must complete before session rows are populated. The added lightweight chat projection is serialized in the same response; transcript/session-channel hydration is not required for the initial catalog title.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and validate each registered session's existing catalog payload
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one payload resolution per registered session, with fallback/reconciliation behavior unchanged; chat metadata is mapped in-memory from that payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalog payload was read to build each session row, but chats were not copied into session metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the cold list path; the diff increases projected response data by the number of catalog chats but does not add database calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: listSessions protocol request/response carrying SessionSummary items
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request/response for the list; payload size now scales with total lightweight chats across returned sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One list response carried session metadata without the per-session chats arrays.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before catalog-backed rows appear; added mapping/serialization is linear in total chat metadata.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered sessions plus total catalog chats after the existing per-session catalog grouping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog sessions retain the existing listing concurrency/grouping; the diff adds in-memory per-chat mapping and no new per-chat boundary call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm provider cache deserializes the same added chat arrays; cold listing reads current catalog payloads. No new negative-cache behavior or per-chat cache miss was introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that boundary count is unchanged and payload/allocation grows linearly with total lightweight chats.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact list sizes and metadata byte counts vary, but the added bounded metadata serialization alone does not establish a reportable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the feature intentionally adds bounded lightweight metadata to the existing batched list response without per-chat I/O fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or observe a catalog-backed peer chat row and hydrate transient details
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial title/interactivity can render from catalog metadata. Observing wrapped title/status/workspace/etc. acquires a session-state lease and asynchronously starts one shared session subscription; hydration is off the initial metadata critical path, but subscription retries remain active while the row observer exists.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to the session state channel and later unsubscribe
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one coalesced subscription per observed session regardless of how many peer fields or rows are observed. On persistent failure, the added microtask retry creates an unbounded sequence of subscribe/unsubscribe pairs for that session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Peer catalog detail observation did not hold a new retry lease, and subscription failure did not immediately re-enter _ensureSessionStateSubscription indefinitely.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not required to display seeded catalog title, but required for live transient status/detail enrichment; failed retries run continuously in the background while observed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of concurrently observed sessions under normal operation; under failure, cost additionally scales with failure duration and rejection speed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ReferenceCollection coalesces all field observers for a session into one live lease, but retries are serialized back-to-back with no delay or backpressure. Different observed sessions may retry independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A live session subscription is reused when present. Errored AgentSubscriptionManager entries are deliberately evicted, so every retry is a cold subscribe rather than a cached failure; there is no negative-cache/backoff state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high; observer acquisition, refcount coalescing, errored-entry eviction, wire subscribe, unsubscribe, and immediate microtask retry were all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure prevalence and remote round-trip latency vary, but the unbounded retry mechanism and boundary calls are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: persistent subscription errors produce an unbounded IPC/network retry stream.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a live session from cached ordered chat metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider metadata resolution and the existing cached catalog/default-chat reads complete before the restored SessionSummary is installed; peer backing/history enrichment remains asynchronous within the existing restore workflow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read cached chat catalog and default-chat working-directory data
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached catalog read per restored session, started earlier and awaited once; one existing default-chat working-directory read. Peer restore work remains grouped through the existing cached catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cached catalog was read later in the restore path and used for default-chat and peer restoration, without seeding summary.chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalog data is awaited before constructing restored chat summaries. Starting cachedChatCatalogPromise earlier overlaps it with existing restore work rather than adding a read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats in one restored session and number of sessions restored by existing callers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The catalog read is newly overlapped with intervening restore work; peer restoration retains its existing Promise-based concurrency and per-session grouping.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold restore reads persisted catalog data once; warm in-memory state is reused by the state manager. Missing catalog data remains undefined and does not cause per-chat retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the single promise creation/await and unchanged _restorePeerChats call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific peer restoration cost varies, but this diff neither adds boundary cardinality nor moves a new call onto the restore path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the changed scheduling overlaps an existing single catalog read and adds only linear in-memory summary mapping.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collapse, expand, recreate, and eventually delete nested sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user collapse/expand event synchronously mutates the in-memory Set and stores a JSON representation in profile storage before the event handler returns; list recreation parses the full stored array at construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy and JSON-serialize every retained collapsed session resource
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-set serialization per changed collapse/expand action; effective cardinality is all historically collapsed resources still retained, including deleted sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-session collapse set or full-set serialization/storage existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously on the UI collapse event and during constructor load/parsing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write profile-scoped collapse JSON through IStorageService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage write per changed collapse/expand, with bytes proportional to the retained historical set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only bounded section collapse state was persisted; deleted per-session resource identities were not retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Performed directly in the collapse event path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Lifetime count of distinct nested sessions the user collapsed and did not later explicitly expand, not the current live-session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Collapse writes are synchronous and uncoalesced, though user actions are naturally serialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The profile value is loaded once into a Set. There is no eviction, LRU bound, or cleanup on session removal; stale entries survive window and application recreation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high; repository references show deletion only on explicit expansion and no pruning in the existing session-removal handler.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large impact requires a long-lived profile and repeated collapse/delete usage, so severity is low despite certain unbounded growth.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: stale collapse identities are retained indefinitely and make future serialization/storage work scale with profile history.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 22 changed files and all diff pages. Two diff-caused issues were submitted: immediate unbounded session-subscription retry while peer details remain observed, and unbounded persisted collapse identities for removed sessions. Existing catalog/restore boundaries remain batched or single-read, and added chat metadata causes linear serialization/allocation without new per-chat I/O fan-out.
